_comment: Every hull in the game. `craft` is the research grade a side must reach before a yard will lay one down; absent means it can be built from the first day. The three with `legend` are the Pirate Lords' ships: they are stories, not hulls, and nobody builds or sails them. Stats not stated here come from the role in constants.ts.

classes.name: Kestrel
classes.blurb: A sloop-of-war. The fastest thing the Crown puts to sea and the first to sink. Good for closing a harbor cheaply.

classes.name: Razorback
classes.blurb: A heavy frigate. Cheap for what it carries, quick enough to be useful, and outmatched by anything of the line.

classes.name: Sovereign
classes.blurb: A first-rate of the line, built straight and coppered to the waterline. Nothing afloat hits harder or takes more killing. Slow to arrive anywhere.

classes.name: Fluyt
classes.blurb: An unarmed merchantman pressed into service. Carries more companies than anything else and cannot defend itself at all.

classes.name: Bulwark
classes.blurb: An armoured frigate: broad, deep, high in the freeboard and built to stand in a line and not move. Fewer guns than a Razorback and half again the hull, which is the whole of the argument for her.

classes.name: Kestrel II
classes.blurb: The Kestrel with her frames doubled and her rig re-cut. Still the first thing the Crown sends to look at something, and no longer the first thing lost doing it. Green sails.

classes.name: Vanguard
classes.blurb: A cruiser built to hunt rather than to hold: nearly a first-rate's broadside on a hull that can catch what it is shooting at. Thinner in the side than a Sovereign, and it shows the moment she has to stand.

classes.name: Razorback II
classes.blurb: The Razorback family, refined: a heavier battery on a better-framed hull, and quick with it. The Admiralty's answer to everything between a sloop and a ship of the line. Green sails.

classes.name: Fluyt II
classes.blurb: A merchantman built for the service from the keel up rather than pressed into it: more hold, more frame, and fast enough to keep up with the fleet she is feeding. Green sails.

classes.name: Vanguard II
classes.blurb: The hunter perfected. She carries a first-rate's weight and sails like a frigate, and there is nothing on the water that can both beat her and catch her. Green sails, gold at the rail.

classes.name: Sovereign II
classes.blurb: Not a new class: the Sovereign, taken as far as the Highwater yards can take her. More gundeck, more frame, more of everything the first one already had too much of. Deep Imperial-green sails.

classes.name: Majestic
classes.blurb: The largest thing the Crown knows how to build. She takes a season to lay down, a fortune to keep, and arrives after the argument is over — but nothing that has ever been in front of her is still there.

classes.name: Swift
classes.blurb: A schooner, stolen and re-rigged. Outruns everything on the water and comes apart if anything catches it.

classes.name: Tempest
classes.blurb: A frigate patched together out of three others. Not pretty. Holds its own against anything short of a ship of the line.

classes.name: Brig
classes.blurb: A blunt-nosed hauler. No guns worth the name, but it lands companies where they are wanted.

classes.name: Reef-class
classes.blurb: Grown, not built — a living coral hull the Reef-folk sing into shape over years. No two alike, enormous, and in no hurry: she is the slowest thing either side puts to sea and she throws more iron at a seawall than anything the Crown has. If a Confederate siege train exists, she is it.

classes.name: Cutlass
classes.blurb: A corvette carrying nearly twice the iron her size has any business with, and a hold full of people who mean to be on your deck. Built around the boarding action: she lands more companies than a frigate does and is no use at all in a line.

classes.name: Reefwalker
classes.blurb: A Shoal-folk cutter: tiny, quiet, and drawing so little water she works reefs a sloop would open herself on. She sees everything and survives nothing.

classes.name: Marauder
classes.blurb: Low, fast, and all of it forward. A raider that hits like a frigate on the way in and cannot take the answer, which is why she is never there for it.

classes.name: Urskin Whaler
classes.blurb: A northern whaling hull with the ice-frames still in her and a harpoon battery over the bow big enough to take a mast out. Slow, enormously hard to kill, and she carries the people to finish it ashore.

classes.name: Freebooter
classes.blurb: What a Confederate yard builds when a captain has the gold to ask for everything: a great human-built cruiser, no two alike, the upper works cut to one person's taste. The Confederacy's answer to a first-rate, and it is not a copy of one.

classes.name: Free Harbor
classes.blurb: Commodore-Elect Adaira Hale's ship: Corwin Calloway's old coral-grown three-decker, named for what he meant her to be, since any deck of his was a free harbor to anyone the Crown wanted. The Moot was called on her quarterdeck and has been the Moot ever since. Where Hale is, the Moot sits — the hull was never the point, and nobody has seen it in years.

classes.name: Swallowtail
classes.blurb: Captain Silas Reyne's coral-grown sloop, which should not be as fast as she is and has never once been caught. Reyne is not off her for a night in his life, so far as anyone tells it, and that is the whole of why he turns up where he does when he does — a week's sail in half a week, every time, and no explanation offered.

classes.name: Ironback
classes.blurb: The Crown dreadnought Admiral Dorian Jessup took with him when he left the Imperium's service, and fought the Crown's own line with for nine years. What he learned aboard her he teaches to whatever squadron is lying in the harbor he is posted to, which is worth more to the Confederacy now than the ship ever was.
